name: Defending
goal: When you are under attack, you can bring defenders, trade off the strongest attacker, give material back, or hit back somewhere else.
intro: When your opponent attacks your king, look for the move that takes the most force out of the attack. Bring a defender closer, offer to trade the strongest attacking piece, or give back material you won earlier if that breaks the attack. And sometimes the best defence is to hit back: a check or a threat that makes the attacker stop and answer you.

parts.title: Bring a defender
parts.keyIdea: Bring a piece back to guard the squares around your king, best of all one that makes a threat as it arrives.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's queen on h3, knight on f4 and rook on g5 have all come close to your king.

notes.text: Bring the bishop home. On f1 it guards g2 and attacks Black's queen, so Black has to stop and move the queen. After a slow move instead, Black would play ...Rh5, lining up rook and queen against your pawn on h2.
Black's queen has been pushed back and your king is safe again, so your own queen can take the undefended pawn on b7.

parts.title: Trade the strongest attacker
parts.keyIdea: Offer to trade the attacking queen: without it, most attacks on the king run out of force.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are Black. White's queen on h6 and knight on h5 are right next to your king, and the queen also eyes your pawn on e6.

notes.text: Offer the queen trade on g5, a square guarded by your rook on g8 and your knight on h7. Either the queens come off, or White's queen has to leave your king.
Take back with the knight. White's attack has lost its queen, and your knight leaves the edge of the board.
Put the knight on e4, a central square that no white pawn can attack. Pushing the a-pawn was also a good move.

parts.title: Give material back
parts.keyIdea: If the material you won has left your king under attack, giving some of it back to break the attack is often best.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White and the exchange up (a rook against a knight), but Black's queen, rook and knight are all close to your king.

notes.text: Your rook on e1 is attacked by Black's queen, and nothing defends it. If Black takes it with check, the attack becomes a mating attack. Give the exchange back instead: take the knight on e4 with the rook.
Take the pawn. The knight has gone, you are still a pawn up, and your queen attacks the rook on f5.
Black defended the rook with g6. Attack it a second time along the fifth rank: now Black is the one who has to defend.

parts.title: Hit back
parts.keyIdea: When defending looks hard, look for a counter-attack: a check that wins time or material can turn the game around.
parts.text: A Lichess Puzzle. You are Black. White's queen has just taken on g7 and now attacks your rook on h8. Before you defend it, look at the e-file.

notes.text: Hit back with check. The knight leaves e5, so your queen on e7 now attacks White's rook on e1, and White has to answer the check first.
Castle long. Your king leaves the centre, and your rook on d8 now guards h8, so Qxh8 is answered by Rxh8. You have won a rook for the knight.
